def: A numbered slot in a compute namespace that holds one program (downloaded or device-defined); commands such as Load Program, Program Activation Management and Execute Program refer to programs by this index.

The Computational Programs step that makes a loaded program at a program index runnable (and deactivation, which makes it not runnable); performed with the Program Activation Management admin command.

The Computational Programs I/O command that runs an activated program on a compute engine against memory ranges in Subsystem Local Memory and returns a program-specific result in the completion; its opcode must be read from the Computational Programs command set specification.
One of the two request contexts of an NVMe-MI management endpoint, selected by a bit in the NMP byte; each slot processes one NVMe-MI command at a time, and Control Primitives act on slots.
A short NVMe-MI message (Pause, Resume, Abort, Get State, Replay) that the management endpoint processes even while a command slot is busy; distinct from the NVMe Abort admin command.

An interim NVMe-MI response status telling the requester that the command is still being processed, with an estimate of the extra time needed; the final response for the same slot follows and the request must not be re-sent.
A PCIe Message TLP whose contents are defined outside the PCIe specification; MCTP uses Type 1 VDMs (per DMTF DSP0238) to carry management packets over the PCIe link.
In the NVMe Boot Firmware Table, an (offset, length) pair that locates variable-length data such as an NQN or address in the table's heap; the offset is counted from the first byte of the table.
In the NBFT, a descriptor for a network interface used by pre-OS firmware for NVMe-oF boot, with transport details such as PCI address, MAC, VLAN, IP configuration and DHCP data.
In the NBFT, a descriptor for one path to an NVMe-oF namespace used at boot: transport type, address, service ID, subsystem NQN, namespace ID, flags and the HFI and discovery entries it uses.
NVMe/TCP ICReq field giving the maximum number of outstanding R2T PDUs per command that the host supports, as a 0's based value (0 means one).
NVMe/TCP ICReq field requesting the alignment, in 4-byte units and 0's based, of data in PDUs the controller sends to the host; the controller pads after the header to meet it.
NVMe/TCP ICResp field giving the alignment, in 4-byte units and 0's based, the controller requires for data in PDUs the host sends.

NVMe/TCP PDU (type 02h) with which the host terminates a connection after a fatal transport error, carrying a Fatal Error Status and a copy of the offending PDU header; C2HTermReq is the controller's equivalent.
Delay of later data on an in-order channel while earlier data is transmitted or recovered; in NVMe/TCP, all commands sharing one TCP connection wait behind large PDUs and behind lost segments.
A secret provisioned on (or derived for) both host and target and used to authenticate a TLS 1.3 session for NVMe/TCP, instead of certificates.
